title: Alfajores (Dulce de Leche Sandwich Cookies)
summary: Soft, melt-in-the-mouth cornflour cookies sandwiched with dulce de leche and finished with a roll of desiccated coconut around the edge.
equipment: 2 large metal baking trays lined with baking paper
stand mixer or electric hand whisk

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
thick dulce de leche (repostero or baking type)

steps.title: Mix the dry ingredients
steps.text: Whisk the cornflour, plain flour, baking powder and salt together in a bowl. Keeping these combined and ready means they mix into the creamed butter evenly in one go.

steps.title: Cream butter and sugar
steps.text: Beat the butter and caster sugar on medium speed for 2-3 minutes until pale, then beat in the egg yolks one at a time, followed by the vanilla and lemon zest. Adding the yolks gradually keeps the mixture smooth rather than curdling.

steps.title: Add the dry mix
steps.text: Add the dry ingredients on low speed and mix only until just combined. The high share of cornflour here is what gives these cookies their signature melting, crumbly texture rather than a chewy one.

steps.title: Chill the dough
steps.text: Pat the dough into two discs, wrap and chill for 1 hour. Chilling firms up the butter so the dough is easier to roll and holds its shape when cut.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C (150°C fan) for at least 20 minutes before baking. A gentle, properly heated oven bakes these pale cookies through without letting them brown.

steps.title: Roll and cut
steps.text: Roll the dough between sheets of baking paper to 5mm thick and cut into 5cm rounds, spacing them 2cm apart. Working between baking paper stops this soft, delicate dough sticking as you roll it.

steps.title: Bake until set but pale
steps.text: Bake one tray at a time for 10-12 minutes, until the cookies are set and dry on top but still pale, with no browning. Staying pale matters here, as any colour means they've dried out too much and will lose their soft, crumbly bite.

steps.title: Cool carefully
steps.text: Cool on the tray for 10 minutes, as the cookies are very fragile straight from the oven, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely. Handling them too soon can crack or crumble them before they've firmed up.

steps.title: Fill and finish
steps.text: Spread about 2 tsp of dulce de leche on half the cookies, top with the remaining cookies and press gently so the filling reaches the edge. Roll the exposed edges in desiccated coconut.

steps.title: Rest before serving
steps.text: Leave the filled cookies to rest for 1 hour; they are even better the next day, once the filling has had time to soften the cookies slightly.

tips: Watch closely near the end of baking - a common mistake is leaving these in too long until they brown, which dries them out instead of keeping them soft and crumbly.
Let the cookies cool fully on the tray before moving them, as they're too fragile to handle while warm.
Use a thick, baking-grade dulce de leche so the filling holds its shape in the sandwich rather than oozing out.
Press gently but firmly when sandwiching so the filling reaches all the way to the edge for an even bite.
If you have time, let the finished alfajores rest overnight rather than just an hour, as they soften and taste even better the next day.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Store filled alfajores in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 4 days, or in the fridge for up to 1 week if your kitchen is warm. Unfilled cookies can be frozen for up to 2 months; fill once thawed.
